title: Jethro Advises Moses to Delegate
text:
After the Israelites left Egypt, Moses' father-in-law Jethro, a priest of Midian, came to visit him in the wilderness, bringing Moses' wife and sons. The two men greeted each other warmly, and Moses told him everything that had happened.

The next day Jethro watched Moses at work. Moses sat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening, waiting for him to settle their disputes and tell them God's laws. Jethro asked him why he sat alone with everyone standing around him all day. Moses explained that the people came to him to inquire of God and to have their cases decided.

Jethro told him plainly that what he was doing was not good. He would surely wear himself out, and the people with him. The task was too heavy for one man. He advised Moses to keep the role of teaching the law and bringing the hardest matters before God, but to choose capable men who feared God, were trustworthy and hated bribes, and appoint them over groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens. They would judge the small cases and bring only the great ones to Moses.

Moses listened and did everything Jethro said. Then Jethro went home to his own country.
lesson: If everything must pass through you, you have become the bottleneck. Choose trustworthy people, give them real authority, and keep for yourself only the decisions only you can make.
